shape.text: Neon's changelog of 2025-01-31 says newly created API keys are prefixed with napi_ so that secret scanning can rely on an identifiable marker, and that existing unprefixed keys stay valid. It states no body length or alphabet.

After napi_ come at least 64 letters and digits, read to the end of the run. One scanner rule matches exactly 64 and a masking library uses 64 as a floor. Two other widely used scanners have no Neon rule, and GitHub secret scanning lists a Neon key type without publishing its expression, which corroborates the prefix only.
Neon's API-keys page describes a key as a randomly generated 64-bit token, which fits no string length, and its only written example is not a shape, so the page is not used for the body.
Keys issued before the prefix was introduced have no marker.

unresolved.reason: The changelog says earlier keys stay valid and carry no marker, but no source describes what they look like.
